extracted_claims.text: As originally enacted, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 provided that obligations for high-risk AI systems (including those listed in Annex III) would become applicable 36 months after entry into force, i.e. 2 August 2026.
Article 113(c) of the AI Act set the application date for Chapter III, Sections 1-3 (covering Annex III high-risk systems) as 2 August 2026 in the originally adopted text.

The European Commission proposed, via a 'Digital Omnibus on AI' (also called AI Omnibus), to delay application of high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months, tying the new start date to confirmation that needed standards and tools are available.

The AI Omnibus legislative proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, a political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026, and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026.
Following the AI Omnibus, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027.
The obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products listed in Annex I (Union harmonisation legislation) apply from 2 August 2028.

The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version dated 27.07.2026) of Article 111(2) no longer references the fixed date '2 August 2026' but instead refers to 'the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113', reflecting the Omnibus amendment.
The AI Act Service Desk's non-consolidated commentary on Article 111 still quotes the pre-Omnibus text, stating the relevant date as 2 August 2026.
The Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, part of the Digital Omnibus on AI, is described as the binding legal instrument that moved the Annex III high-risk deadline from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027.

2 August 2026 remains the application date for other AI Act obligations (e.g., Article 50 transparency duties, AI literacy requirements, prohibitions) even though the Annex III high-risk deadline was pushed back.

Some commentary describes 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 as 'backstop dates' that would apply only if the Commission's proposed Omnibus amendments were not approved before 2 August 2026, implying uncertainty prior to the Omnibus's entry into force.

Several news/legal-analysis sources published before the Omnibus's entry into force (or not accounting for it) continue to describe 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations.
Providers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III must meet requirements in Articles 8 to 15 of the AI Act and complete a conformity assessment before placing a system on the market.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally enacted, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 required obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [EU AI Act Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)). However, a subsequent "Digital Omnibus on AI" amendment, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, pushed this deadline back by roughly 16 months, meaning Annex III obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy - AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Significant source confusion remains, as many pre-Omnibus legal and industry analyses still cite the original 2 August 2026 date without reflecting this amendment.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (As Enacted)
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 set 2 August 2026 — 36 months after entry into force — as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations, including those under Annex III (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [AI Act Law - Article 113](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). Specifically, Article 113(c) designated this date for Chapter III, Sections 1–3, which govern Annex III high-risk systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Law - Article 113](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The European Commission proposed a "Digital Omnibus on AI" to delay high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months, conditioning the new timeline on confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools were available (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The legislative process moved through adoption on 19 November 2025, political agreement between Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and entry into force of the amending regulation on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy - Regulatory Framework](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Current Applicable Dates
Following the Omnibus, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence), as confirmed across multiple EU guidance sources ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI embedded in regulated products under Annex I apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). Notably, 2 August 2026 remains the applicable date for other AI Act provisions unaffected by the delay, including Article 50 transparency duties, AI literacy requirements, and prohibitions on certain AI practices (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq), [EU AI Compass Timeline](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version dated 27.07.2026) confirms this change: Article 111(2) no longer cites the fixed "2 August 2026" date but instead refers to "the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113" (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Some sources identify the amending instrument as "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," though this citation carries low confidence given limited corroboration (low confidence) ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A substantial contradiction exists between sources published before versus after the Omnibus's entry into force. Numerous legal-analysis and industry blog sources continue to state 2 August 2026 as the operative Annex III deadline (low confidence), apparently not accounting for the Omnibus amendment ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)), while EU guidance sources consistently report the extended 2 December 2027 date.

The AI Act Service Desk's own Article 111 commentary still quotes the pre-Omnibus 2 August 2026 date, creating an internal inconsistency with the consolidated EUR-Lex text (medium confidence vs. high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

One source describes a different transition date (August 2, 2027) for Annex I regulated-product systems, conflicting with the 2 August 2028 date reported elsewhere; this appears to be an error (low confidence) ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)).

Some commentary frames 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 as contingent "backstop" dates rather than fixed deadlines, a characterization carrying low confidence (0.12) ([LinkedIn - Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)).

## Knowledge Gaps
The precise legal citation and Official Journal publication status of the amending Omnibus regulation remain unconfirmed. It is unclear whether the 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 dates are truly final or still contingent on conditions such as availability of harmonised standards. The interaction between Article 111 (systems already on the market) and the revised Article 113 timeline requires clarification, given inconsistencies in EU guidance itself. Additional implementing or delegated acts may be needed before 2 December 2027 to operationalize Annex III obligations, but this remains unconfirmed.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally enacted, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 required obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [EU AI Act Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)). However, a subsequent "Digital Omnibus on AI" amendment, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, pushed this deadline back by roughly 16 months, meaning Annex III obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy - AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Significant source confusion remains, as many pre-Omnibus legal and industry analyses still cite the original 2 August 2026 date without reflecting this amendment.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (As Enacted)
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 set 2 August 2026 — 36 months after entry into force — as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations, including those under Annex III (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [AI Act Law - Article 113](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). Specifically, Article 113(c) designated this date for Chapter III, Sections 1–3, which govern Annex III high-risk systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Law - Article 113](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The European Commission proposed a "Digital Omnibus on AI" to delay high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months, conditioning the new timeline on confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools were available (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The legislative process moved through adoption on 19 November 2025, political agreement between Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and entry into force of the amending regulation on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy - Regulatory Framework](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Current Applicable Dates
Following the Omnibus, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence), as confirmed across multiple EU guidance sources ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI embedded in regulated products under Annex I apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). Notably, 2 August 2026 remains the applicable date for other AI Act provisions unaffected by the delay, including Article 50 transparency duties, AI literacy requirements, and prohibitions on certain AI practices (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq), [EU AI Compass Timeline](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version dated 27.07.2026) confirms this change: Article 111(2) no longer cites the fixed "2 August 2026" date but instead refers to "the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113" (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Some sources identify the amending instrument as "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," though this citation carries low confidence given limited corroboration (low confidence) ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A substantial contradiction exists between sources published before versus after the Omnibus's entry into force. Numerous legal-analysis and industry blog sources continue to state 2 August 2026 as the operative Annex III deadline (low confidence), apparently not accounting for the Omnibus amendment ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)), while EU guidance sources consistently report the extended 2 December 2027 date.

The AI Act Service Desk's own Article 111 commentary still quotes the pre-Omnibus 2 August 2026 date, creating an internal inconsistency with the consolidated EUR-Lex text (medium confidence vs. high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

One source describes a different transition date (August 2, 2027) for Annex I regulated-product systems, conflicting with the 2 August 2028 date reported elsewhere; this appears to be an error (low confidence) ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)).

Some commentary frames 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 as contingent "backstop" dates rather than fixed deadlines, a characterization carrying low confidence (0.12) ([LinkedIn - Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)).

## Knowledge Gaps
The precise legal citation and Official Journal publication status of the amending Omnibus regulation remain unconfirmed. It is unclear whether the 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 dates are truly final or still contingent on conditions such as availability of harmonised standards. The interaction between Article 111 (systems already on the market) and the revised Article 113 timeline requires clarification, given inconsistencies in EU guidance itself. Additional implementing or delegated acts may be needed before 2 December 2027 to operationalize Annex III obligations, but this remains unconfirmed.
